result.summary: This PR adds util::ResultPtr, a wrapper around util::Result for functions that return a pointer, so callers can write result->member instead of (*result)->member, and so a successful result containing a null pointer evaluates false in boolean context instead of true. It converts several call sites to the new type: wallet createWallet/loadWallet/restoreWallet, LoadAddrman, and the kernel's chainstate loading. It is layered on top of the still-open util::Result rework in #25665 and carries that PR's chainstate load-status refactor along with it, plus a CI false-positive fix and expanded result_tests.cpp coverage.
result.problem: Code using util::Result<std::unique_ptr<T>> has to double-dereference and, worse, a successful result holding a null pointer reads as truthy, a footgun the author opened as issue #26004. Wallet-loading and addrman-loading call sites currently carry this risk.

open_concerns: l0rinc (2026-07-23) questioned whether the ternary in restoreWallet (`wallet && !error.empty() ? std::move(wallet) : util::Error{error}`) is inverted; this looks like a real bug since it returns the wallet as success only when an error string is also present. No visible reply or fix in the shown diff despite later force-pushes on 2026-08-15 and 2026-09-08.
The PR is a partial solution to #26004 by the author's own admission; a full fix would need a not_null-style type (tracked in #24423), which is not part of this PR.

result.card: This PR adds util::ResultPtr, a syntax-sugar wrapper around util::Result for pointer-returning functions, and applies it to wallet loading, addrman loading, and kernel chainstate loading. It fixes a real latent-bug pattern: a successful Result holding a null pointer previously evaluated as truthy, which the author tracks as issue #26004; ResultPtr makes such a result evaluate false instead. It is stacked on the still-open base PR #25665 and has been rebased over twenty times across four years without merging. A reviewer (l0rinc) flagged what looks like inverted success/error logic in the restoreWallet code this PR touches, and that concern appears unaddressed through later force-pushes. Only one reviewer has engaged substantively; there is no broader concept discussion. The change is foundational plumbing feeding several of the author's other in-flight PRs (#29700, #30342) rather than a user-facing feature.
